editorial:
Imagine growing up with a dad who is more interested in old books than his own daughter. That is exactly what you get with Fanny and her father, Hubert. He is a brilliant academic, but he has been stuck in the past ever since his wife died twelve years ago. The vibe starts off slow and a bit sad, but everything flips when a hidden family secret suddenly pops up. You will feel Fanny's urgency as she stops being a passive observer and starts hunting for the truth about her mother's death. It turns into a race against time that keeps you guessing about who is actually lying.

What really works here is how the mystery unfolds. The acting feels real, and the twists do not feel forced. While some parts of the middle drag a bit, the payoff at the end makes it worth it. You should definitely check this out if you love stories about family secrets and detective work.
endingExplained: You will find out that Fanny's mother did not die in a simple accident. The big twist reveals that her father, Hubert, hid the truth to protect Fanny from a dangerous family rival. In the final scenes, Fanny finds the missing letters that prove her mother was actually silenced by a greedy relative. Once the truth comes out, Hubert and Fanny finally heal their relationship and find peace together after years of silence.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family mysteries and emotional journeys.
